newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs off $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by adequate hog supplies and slowing packer demand going into the Easter holiday weekend, livestock dealers said.

At least one interior Iowa/southern Minnesota major packer reported having the hogs needed for slaughter through Friday. Several plants also will be closed on Monday in observance of the Easter holiday on Sunday, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 lower at $48.00 to $49.50 in the country and $50.00 to $50.50 at plants, they said.
USDA confirmed the Iowa/southern Minnesota hog run at 128,000 head Wednesday sharply exceeded the 110,000-head estimate.

Illinois hogs sold $1.00 lower at $48.50 to $50.00 in the country and $50.50 to $51.00 at plants. Packers had been paying a premium for hogs that put the top plant price $1.00 higher than USDA top price quotes, sources there said.
The Illinois top plant price early Thursday was now in-line with $51.00 quoted by USDA on Wednesday, dealers said.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 lower at $48.50 to $49.00 in the country and up to $50.00 at plants. Ohio hogs sold $1.00 lower at $46.00 to $47.00 in the country and $48.00 to $49.00 plants. Prices at Indiana/Ohio locations were pressured by large hog movement, the dealers said.
